chunks: Muhammad ibn Muslim narrated from Abī Jaʿfar عليه السلام, who said:

There is no headcovering required upon the slave woman in salat (prayer), nor upon the mudabbarah is there a headcovering in salat (prayer), nor upon the mukatabah, if her master has stipulated that upon her, a headcovering in salat (prayer), while she remains owned until she completes all of her contract of manumission; and there applies to her whatever applies to the owned slave in all legal penalties.

key_terms.الْمُدَبَّرَةِ: a slave woman designated for emancipation upon her master's death
key_terms.الْمُكَاتَبَةِ: a slave woman under a contractual manumission agreement
key_terms.مَمْلُوكَةٌ: remaining in the state of being owned

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on headcovering for a slave woman, mudabbarah, or mukatabah in salat (prayer)?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a fiqh ruling regarding the dress requirements of certain categories of enslaved women in salat (prayer). It also states that the mukatabah remains under the legal status of ownership until she fully completes her manumission contract, and the rulings applying to the owned slave continue to apply to her.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: Hadith.1085 - Muhammad ibn Muslim narrated from Imam Muhammad ibn Ali Al-Baqir (as) who said:

"There is no obligation for a slave woman (amā) to wear a headcover (qina'ah) in prayer, nor for a woman who is 'mukātabah' (a slave who has entered into a contract to pay for her freedom) if her master has not required it as part of the terms of her contract, until She has fulfilled all the terms of her contract. The same rules that apply to a slave in all legal matters apply to her as well."
